solver.kind: blind AI solver (separate agent, answer-free packet, rubric v2)

S028-01.notes: Sprout, bloom, seed within weeks then vanish = short-lived, ephemeral. 'Dormant' is a plausible trap (describes the between-rain state, not the plants' striking trait); 'perennial' is the opposite. Vocabulary level of 'ephemeral' keeps it out of easy.

S028-02.notes: Understated 'interesting' and stressing unknowns = restrained. Dismissive is the only mild distractor; she doesn't belittle the result.

flags: minor: underlining is conveyed only via the stem parenthetical; ensure the rendered item actually underlines the sentence
S028-03.notes: Sentence flags that the synchronized emergence has a reason, which the next sentence explains (predator satiation). Facts on 13/17-year periodical cicadas and predator satiation are accurate.

S028-04.notes: Regular, identical periodic dips rule out random surface change; a transiting planet is the logical inference. A contradicts the passage; B and C unsupported. Transit duration/period realistic.

flags: minor: choice A is telegraphic compared with the other choices ('Bags fell 70 percent; ...'); consider a fuller sentence for parallel style
S028-05.notes: Bags 300->90 = 70%; bottles 420->210 = 50%; butts 650->600 = 7.7% (~8%). All verified. Only A compares percentages across all types. B (equal absolute drops) and D (lowest count) are traps that don't address percentage decrease.

S028-06.notes: Text 2 says shared workshop style makes hands indistinguishable and parchment differs in the last third, undercutting the single-scribe inference from consistent letters. A contradicts; B (date) and D (authorship of sermons vs copying) are unsupported.

S028-07.notes: 'Herders' is the plural subject of 'drive'; no possession. Plural verb 'drive' rules out singular herder's. Possessive traps catch some students, but this is a routine one-step check.

S028-08.notes: Colon introduces the 'one thing' that follows, a noun phrase. Semicolon needs an independent clause after it; comma is weak/ambiguous here and SAT treats colon as the precise choice; ', it was' creates a comma splice.

S028-09.notes: Inefficient yet transformative = contrast, so 'Nonetheless.' Historical claim (Newcomen engines pumping water from British mines despite low efficiency) is accurate.

S028-10.notes: Only C makes a recommendation ('the district should...'); others just restate notes.
